summary.headline: Costco presented detailed plans for a 167,000-square-foot store and gas station on Coslin Drive, drawing questions on traffic and noise.
summary.summary: The Planning Board opened its public hearing on a major site plan and special permits for a proposed Costco warehouse and 15-pump fueling station at 21 Coslin Drive, focusing on traffic, landscaping, and site access. The board also reviewed proposed revisions to a Town Meeting warrant article on two-family dwellings, continuing the hearing to a pre-Town Meeting session. Additionally, the board examined Fay School landscape mitigation plans and received an update from the Master Plan Implementation Committee on planning for Master Plan 2030.

topics.title: Two-family dwelling zoning bylaw warrant article
topics.summary: The board continued its public hearing on the Zoning Board of Appeals warrant article regarding two-family dwellings. ZBA representative Doris explained that the Select Board had reopened and closed the warrant to incorporate minor text cleanup, including deleting references to townhouse and duplex and fixing redundant language. A former Planning Board chair raised concerns that wording on district lot sizes could unintentionally permit two-family dwellings on smaller commercial lots, prompting discussion about whether the ZBA or Planning Board should sponsor a floor amendment at Town Meeting.
key_details: Language removing townhouse and duplex definitions was adopted by the ZBA.
A former Planning Board chair argued the current draft might bypass residential lot size requirements in business districts.
The board debated whether to bring an amendment to Town Meeting floor or hold another ZBA coordination meeting.
Town Meeting warrant article hearing was continued to the morning of Town Meeting.
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to October 17, 2026 at 9:05 AM.
topics.why_it_matters: Changes to the town's zoning bylaw govern where and on what lot sizes two-family homes can be built throughout Southborough.

topics.title: 154 Turnpike Road site plan modification
topics.summary: The applicant requested a continuation of the public hearing for non-compliance modifications to a major site plan at 154 Turnpike Road. The board voted to continue the hearing and extend its statutory deadline to act.
key_details: Applicant representative requested continuation without testimony.
Draft decision is expected at the next session.
Statutory action deadline extended to October 23, 2026.
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to October 19, 2026 at 6:45 PM; action deadline extended to October 23, 2026.

topics.title: 22 Turnpike Road (Golf Range) site plan modification
topics.summary: The applicant requested a continuation without testimony for the major site plan modification at the 22 Turnpike Road golf range.
key_details: Applicant engineer requested continuation to the next meeting.
A draft decision will be prepared for the board's review.
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to October 19, 2026 at 6:30 PM.

topics.title: 21 Coslin Drive Costco wholesale warehouse and fuel station
topics.summary: The board opened the public hearing on applications by Costco Wholesale Corporation for major site plan approval, a lower impact development special permit, and a highway major retail special permit for 21 Coslin Drive. The project spans 26.12 acres across Southborough and Westborough and proposes a 167,000-square-foot retail warehouse and a 15-pump fueling facility with 30 dispensing positions. Project consultants presented overviews of site layout, grading, utilities, stormwater wetlands, dark-sky compliant 36-foot light poles, native landscaping, and traffic generation, after which board members and residents raised concerns about traffic congestion, loading dock noise, truck routes, and regional cut-throughs.
key_details: Proposed 167,000-square-foot building with 891 parking spaces and a 15-pump gas station holding up to 60 stacking vehicles.
Site sits on 26.12 acres: 17.8 acres in Southborough and about 8 acres in Westborough.
Estimated trip generation includes 1,238 weekday evening peak trips and 1,666 Saturday midday peak trips.
Traffic mitigation proposed at Route 9 and Crystal Pond Road includes restriping and signal retiming, with MassDOT discussions ongoing.
Town peer review consultants are currently reviewing stormwater and traffic studies, with traffic review due around October 9.
topics.outcome: Public hearing continued to October 19, 2026 at 7:00 PM.
topics.why_it_matters: This major regional retail project would bring substantial economic activity, tax revenue, traffic volume, and infrastructure impacts along the Route 9 corridor.

topics.title: Fay School building addition landscape mitigation plan
topics.summary: Representatives from Fay School presented an updated landscape mitigation plan required as a condition of their building addition approval. The plan proposes planting a mix of native trees, shrubs, and groundcovers along a hillside and fence line to create a pollinator garden. The board and town staff discussed plant selections, ensuring straight native species are used, and pending engineering peer review of as-built site plans.
key_details: Plan proposes eight shrubs in 10-gallon pots and 106 groundcover plants on a hillside near the primary school building.
School previously planted an Eastern Redbud and a Serviceberry on campus.
Town peer reviewer Fuss & O'Neill is reviewing revised as-built civil utility plans.
Discussion of non-neonicotinoid pesticide requirements and plant species list.

topics.title: Master Plan Implementation Committee update and Master Plan 2030
topics.summary: A board member presented recommendations from the Master Plan Implementation Committee regarding preparations for the town's next comprehensive plan, Master Plan 2030. The committee recommended establishing a Master Plan sub-committee in 2027 and considering funding in FY28 for a hybrid approach using a consultant and volunteer committees.
key_details: Current Master Plan was adopted in 2021 and has a 10-year horizon.
Committee recommends creating a Master Plan Sub-Committee in 2027.
Recommended pursuing consultant funding in FY28 for an RFP process.
A joint meeting with the full Master Plan Implementation Committee is planned for October 19, 2026.
topics.outcome: Joint discussion scheduled with the Master Plan Implementation Committee on October 19, 2026.

topics.title: Town Planner report and department updates
topics.summary: The town planner reviewed administrative matters, including an upcoming multi-board meeting on October 8 regarding Elementary School Building Committee options. The Attorney General approved 2026 Annual Town Meeting zoning bylaws with minor guidance. Updates were also provided on commercial drone delivery proposals in Westborough, DPW tree plantings, a ZBA frontage variance at 0 Northborough Road, and ongoing revisions to subdivision regulations.
key_details: Multi-board meeting on elementary school building options set for October 8 at 6:30 PM at the Public Safety Building.
Attorney General approved 2026 ATM zoning bylaws; a minor cross-reference typo will be corrected at a future Town Meeting.
Westborough is reviewing Amazon commercial drone delivery operations that include portions of Southborough within a 7.5-mile delivery radius.
ZBA granted a variance for frontage at 0 Northborough Road despite planning and town counsel concerns about access over state DCR land.
Subdivision rules and regulations update remains in progress.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved minutes from August 17, 2026, and approved amended minutes from September 14, 2026.
key_details: August 17, 2026 minutes approved 3-0-1 with one abstention.
September 14, 2026 minutes approved as amended 3-0-1 with one abstention.

Continue the public hearing for 154 Turnpike Road to October 19, 2026 at 6:45 PM.
Continue the public hearing on 22 Turnpike Road to October 19, 2026 at 6:30 PM.
Extend the Planning Board action deadline for 154 Turnpike Road to October 23, 2026.
Continue the public hearing for 21 Coslin Drive (Costco) to October 19, 2026 at 7:00 PM.

public_comment.summary: A resident expressed confusion about varying map orientations in presentations, highlighted chronic truck accidents damaging guardrails at the Route 85 intersection, and urged the applicant to coordinate with MassDOT on truck turning solutions.

A Flagg Road resident expressed concern about heavy traffic spillover and failing levels of service at Flagg Road and Route 9, asking the peer review to evaluate north-bound cut-through traffic into town, water pressure impacts, and truck route details.

A resident asked whether the traffic study accounted for cumulative traffic from new housing developments in Hopkinton, Ashland, and Holliston that will cut through Southborough, and raised concerns regarding vehicle emissions and air quality at congested intersections.

A resident and biodiversity advocate reviewed the Fay School landscape mitigation plan, emphasizing the need for neonicotinoid pesticide-free certification, straight native plant species, and caution regarding invasive plants like porcelain berry.
